story.title: What Is This Record?
story.teaser: Not every research request comes back with a story in it. Here is what showed up instead.
story.takeaway: Nothing here is a claim about the decoy effect — fact-checking returned only placeholders, so this page records that gap instead of papering over it.

hero.standfirst: You're here because a story about the decoy effect was requested. What came back from fact-checking was a verdict of "revise" and a findings package where the claim, the basis, the turn, the contested question and the unknown all read the literal word "test." [Context] does not publish a story ahead of its paper, and it does not write a paper around findings that were never actually checked. So this page exists instead of both.

blocks.h: What you'd expect to find here
p: Click through to a page named after a psychology term and you expect the usual: a founding study, a number, a mechanism, maybe a menu or a subscription tier used as the working example. The research plan behind this topic sketches exactly that shape — a study from 1982 that named the effect, a pricing experiment, a later argument about how well it replicates outside the lab. None of that is a bad plan. It just never came back as a checked finding.

blocks.h: Not every research request comes back with a story in it. Here is what showed up instead.

blocks.caption: Every field in the package that was supposed to carry evidence carries the word "test" instead.

blocks.h: The one thing actually in the package
p: Every field meant to carry a fact — the claim, its basis, the turn, the contested question, the unknown — carries the word "test" instead. Not a thin finding about the decoy effect. A placeholder that never got swapped for one.

blocks.text: A paper cannot be earned by a story that was never checked.

spec.title: Plan vs. package
spec.sub: what was proposed is not what was graded

blocks.caption: The left column is what the plan proposed. The right is all that's approved to build on — and it's empty.

p: One finding came back, and it read "test." So did the one contested question and the one unknown attached to it — three fields, three placeholders, zero usable. The action isn't to guess at a plausible-sounding number for the decoy effect; it's to send this topic back through fact-checking and hold the page until a real finding, with a source and an error bar, comes back in its place.

zoomout.text: Every other page here carries a paper with named sources behind the story. This one carries a findings file where every field reads "test" — the trace a pipeline leaves when one stage gets skipped and the next one won't guess on its behalf.

paper.title: What Is This Record: the research
paper.subtitle: A paper with nothing yet to report
paper.abstract: This paper cannot make any claims about the decoy effect. The graded-findings package received for this topic returned a verdict of "revise" and consisted entirely of placeholder values: one finding, one contested question, and one unknown, each literally recorded as "test." No real source, number, or mechanism was fact-checked and approved for use. Per house rules, only fact-checker-approved findings may appear in [Context] work, and nothing is stated more confidently in a story than in its paper. This document records that gap rather than filling it with content drawn from the research plan's unverified background notes.

paper.method: No writing method was applied beyond transcription, because there was no verified content to write from. The research plan for this topic named real-sounding sources — a 1982 paper on asymmetric dominance, a subscription-pricing experiment, later meta-analyses and failed replications — but those appeared only in the plan's own rationale, before fact-checking, and were not present in the graded findings handed to the writer. The bias risk this avoids is the most common failure mode in this pipeline: treating a promising plan as if it were an approved finding and writing confident prose around it. The correct next step is to send this topic back through fact-checking and re-run the writing step once real findings, claims, and sources come back graded.
reading: The only input the writer is authorized to draw from; every field in it is a placeholder rather than a checked fact.
